title: Cicala question corpus
description: Each language stores one mixed corpus in questions/{lang}/questions.yaml. Depth and tone permissions govern automatic play.

id.description: q- + first 8 hex chars of SHA-256 of `lang|normalized text`. Assigned by validate.py --fix, never hand-written. Stable forever once assigned; later edits do not change it.

text.description: The question. 10-140 characters, must end with a configured terminator plus an optional closing quote or bracket, no newlines, no leading/trailing whitespace.

depth.description: Editorial exposure cost: 1 asks little public exposure, 2 asks for a personal construction, 3 may ask for vulnerability, conflict, fear, loss, or consequential disclosure. It is independent of tone.

tags.description: Optional editorial tags. dark marks macabre or disturbing material; sexual marks sexual experiences, desires or explicit material. Depth 3 requires the independent Heavy permission.

origin.description: Optional lineage link to an existing question in another language. Languages remain independent corpora.

translated_by.description: Machine-translation provenance. `google` marks a Google Cloud Translation draft or a reviewed descendant of one; it requires `origin`. A later human edit may seed synchronization of the linked translations.

translation_sync.description: CI synchronization receipt. origin retains the human-written lineage anchor; source identifies the version used for this update. Material revisions cover text, depth and tags and prevent generated updates from triggering another round.

author.description: Optional free-text credit. Courtesy only, no legal claim; all questions are CC0.

added.description: ISO date the entry was merged. Set by validate.py --fix.

x-cicala.description: Project config consumed by the validation and build tools. The direct GitHub issue form restates the editorial vocabulary; native website suggestions leave depth and tags to maintainers. `depthLabels` are the exact option strings of the issue form's depth dropdown, indexed by depth minus one. Not part of the JSON Schema vocabulary.
depthLabels: 3 - vulnerability, conflict, fear, loss, or consequential disclosure
